title: Rafael Mouallem Rosa
text:
I am a researcher at Inria, in the Statify team in Grenoble, France. My research is in Bayesian statistics, with applications to statistical learning and macroeconomics.
My current work develops the Sources of Uncertainty (SoU) framework for Bayesian inference. SoU allows different components of a statistical model to be assigned different levels of confidence, providing a way to control their probabilistic treatment and how uncertainty is propagated across the model. This flexibility offers a new tool for Bayesian model design.
I explore applications of this framework to sparse estimation and model selection, Bayesian neural networks, and macroeconomic inference. I hold a Ph.D. in Economics from the São Paulo School of Economics (FGV), was a visiting scholar in the Department of Economics at Harvard University, and previously worked in quantitative finance.

Rafael Mouallem Rosa, Julyan Arbel, and Hien Duy Nguyen (2026). Working paper.

Rafael Mouallem Rosa (2026). Manuscript.
An application of the SoU approach to Bayesian vector autoregressions and the analysis of macroeconomic relationships.
SoU-RHS: Bayesian Structured Sparsity for Compact Architecture Recovery in CNNs
Rafael Mouallem Rosa and Julyan Arbel (2026). Manuscript.
Develops structured Bayesian sparsity at the filter level to recover compact convolutional neural network architectures.

title: Rafael Mouallem Rosa
text:
I am a postdoctoral researcher at Inria working on Bayesian inference, model uncertainty, and statistical learning.
My current research develops the Sources of Uncertainty framework, an extension of Bayesian inference that allows researchers to model different degrees of confidence across components of a probabilistic model. This perspective connects ideas from decision theory, generalized Bayes, variational inference, and modern machine learning.
A central goal of my work is to develop Bayesian methods that remain useful when model uncertainty is not just a technical detail, but a core part of the problem. Recent applications include sparse Bayesian learning, global-local shrinkage methods, and self-pruning Bayesian neural networks.
Before joining Inria, I completed a Ph.D. in Economics, working on decision theory, and later worked in financial markets as a quantitative portfolio manager. This background shapes my interest in statistical methods for high-dimensional, uncertain, and decision-relevant environments.

title: Research
text:
My research focuses on Bayesian inference, model uncertainty, and statistical learning.
The central question in my current work is how Bayesian inference should be modified when the researcher has different degrees of confidence in different components of a probabilistic model. This question connects decision theory, generalized Bayes, variational inference, and modern machine learning.


I develop the Sources of Uncertainty framework, which extends Bayesian inference by assigning confidence parameters to different components of a probabilistic model.
The framework separates two ideas that are usually intertwined:

the informativeness of a prior;
the confidence assigned to the source of uncertainty represented by that prior.

This provides an additional modelling tool for controlling posterior concentration and regularisation.



Building on the Sources of Uncertainty framework, I study sparsity-inducing Bayesian methods based on global-local prior structures.
This leads to SoU-SGL, a sparse global-local estimator designed to recover sparse representations rather than merely shrink parameters toward zero.



I am also interested in Bayesian deep learning, especially methods that allow neural networks to adapt their effective architecture to the data.
Recent work applies the SoU framework to Bayesian neural networks, where it induces self-pruning and can lead to compact architectures without sacrificing predictive performance.

title: Research
text:
My current research develops the Sources of Uncertainty framework for Bayesian inference and explores its applications. The framework draws inspiration from decision-theoretic ideas about uncertainty.


Bayesian inference represents uncertainty through subjective probability distributions. The Sources of Uncertainty framework starts from the observation that the researcher may have different degrees of confidence in different parts of this probabilistic specification.
The framework incorporates this distinction by associating each component of a factorized prior with a confidence parameter. This allows the researcher to specify not only prior beliefs, but also the degree of confidence assigned to each source of uncertainty.
The confidence mechanism operates differently from standard prior informativeness, providing a new modelling lever and greater flexibility in how the posterior is shaped.



Building on the Sources of Uncertainty framework, I propose SoU-SGL, a sparsity-inducing Bayesian method based on global-local prior structures.
While standard global-local priors mainly induce shrinkage, SoU-SGL uses source-specific confidence to push irrelevant components more sharply toward zero.



I apply these ideas to Bayesian neural networks, using structured sparsity to recover compact architectures.
In current work on convolutional neural networks, the procedure identifies compact architectures with similar total size and layer-wise allocation across different starting widths. These architectures maintain competitive accuracy with standard deterministic neural networks while improving probabilistic performance.
